rounds.text: Ashapura Logistics Ltd is heavily discounted by the market, trading at an attractive price-to-earnings ratio of just 11.7x [E1] which sits well below the sector benchmark P/E of 20.32x [E6]. This undervaluation is further underscored by a price-to-book ratio of 0.64x against a book value of ₹ 87.1 per share [E2], representing a steep discount to the sector benchmark P/B of 1.51x [E7]. The company demonstrates solid cash generation fundamentals, posting a robust operating cash flow of Rs 20 Cr in Mar 2026 [E27] that represents 96% of operating profit [E29] and results in an impressive cash conversion rate of 3.33x where profits are fully backed by cash [E26]. Operational efficiency is also improving over the medium term, with the operating margin expanding by 1 percentage point to reach 9% in Mar 2026 compared to 8% three years earlier [E22]. Conceded: the stock currently offers a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4], sits low at 15% of its 52-week range [E5], and experienced a quarter-over-quarter operating margin contraction of 2 percentage points in Mar 2026 [E23] alongside a free cash flow figure of Rs -18 Cr [E28].

Ashapura Logistics Ltd carries structural financial risks that are underscored by severe cash burn, despite apparent headline discounts [E28]. The company generated a negative free cash flow of Rs -18 Cr in Mar 2026, revealing that capital demands heavily outweigh incoming cash despite a reported operating cash flow of Rs 20 Cr [E27, E28]. Furthermore, short-term margin compression is visible as the quarterly operating margin dropped to 8% in Mar 2026 from 10% in the year-ago quarter [-2 percentage points] [E23]. Shareholder returns are entirely absent, demonstrated by a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4], while the market has punished the stock by leaving it depressed at just 15% of the way up its 52-week range [E5]. Conceded: the business maintains an inexpensive valuation trading at a P/E of 11.7x alongside a price-to-book of 0.64x [E1, E2].

Conceded: the company paid no dividends with a yield of 0.00% [E4] and sits low at 15% of its 52-week range [E5]. However, the bear's focus on negative free cash flow of Rs -18 Cr [E28] ignores the robust underlying Rs 20 Cr in operating cash flow generated in Mar 2026 [E27], which represents a stellar 96% conversion of operating profit [E29] and an overall cash conversion rate of 3.33x against reported profit [E26]. While quarterly margins contracted by two percentage points year-over-year [E23], the longer-term trend shows expanding operating profitability, climbing from 8% three years ago to 9% in Mar 2026 [E22]. Furthermore, the market's heavy discount provides a significant margin of safety, with a P/E of 11.7x [E1] and a price-to-book of 0.64x [E2] that trade at deep discounts to sector benchmarks of 20.32x and 1.51x respectively [E6, E7].
